text:
Owen: Noticed an uptick in fragmentation during last night's off-peak reclaim. Several GPU nodes in us-central2 had pinned warm allocations after a failed kubelet upgrade.
Mei: Logs show kubelet restarted but IP tables restoration stalled due to a config helm hook timeout. netlink showed 'carrier lost' around the same time.
Carlos: ops-bot flagged switch-slab errors on rack-2 at 01:02 UTC.
ops-bot: switch/rack-2 slab_err incremented (count=18) 1 01:02:05 - attached to INC-2036.
Rina: paste from scheduler snapshot: 
```
NodeState: node-usc2-056 warmpool_protected=true age=48m
Scheduler: compacting skipped because node.network_health=DEGRADED
Lease: handshake_attempts=6 last_success=2024-10-15T00:11:02Z
Kubelet: restart_count=1 iptables_restore=timeout(30s)
```
Theo: Proposed short-term: run a force-reclaim script that only targets nodes with kubelet_restart_count>0 and net_health==DEGRADED, with manual sign-off from ops.
Owen: Force-reclaim is a good emergency lever. Long-term we should detect hv switch flaps earlier and back off warmpool lock sooner.
Mei: I'm concerned about aggressive force-reclaim causing tenant noise. We need a circuit-breaker and an audit trail.
Carlos: Ops can automate sign-off when net counters are above threshold and the reclaim won't breach tenant QoS (check quota).
Rina: I'll add an event in the console: "Emergency reclaim initiated" with affected pods and node list.
Theo: Will prototype the force-reclaim runbook and add a toggle in the scheduler's admin API.
Owen: Action items: Carlos attach INC-2036, Theo prototype runbook + API toggle, Rina add console event, Mei verify kubelet restore race conditions.
ops-bot: scheduled maintenance window for rack-2 in 15m to clear switch slab errors.
Mei: Thanks - rolling patch to kubelets will wait until after the maintenance to avoid mass restarts.
